unavailable.brenda: data is CC BY 4.0, but the download requires actively ticking the licence box on brenda-enzymes.org/download.php -- an acceptance that has to be made by a person, not a script
unavailable.sabio_rk: REST service returns the web application, not data, from this network
unavailable.fireprotdb: documented API paths return 404; endpoint needs confirming
unavailable.rhea: direct JSON blocked (403); Rhea ids are captured via UniProt instead

surveyed_and_rejected.kaggle: searched via the public API, which needs no token. 'plastic degrading enzyme' returns nothing; 'shrapnel' returns a satellite-telemetry set; 'PETase' returns two datasets under a kilobyte with licence 'Unknown'; 'clinical trials' returns stale dumps of ClinicalTrials.gov, which this project queries live by NCT id. Nothing here carries provenance the engine could attach an Observation to
surveyed_and_rejected.meltome_atlas: real, reachable, well documented -- ProteomicsDB exposes an OData API and PRIDE holds the raw data (PXD011929). It covers 13 model species. The warehouse holds 360 organisms, mostly environmental isolates, compost metagenomes and soil bacteria, so the overlap with our enzymes is close to zero. Worth revisiting only if the engine ever ranks enzymes from model organisms
surveyed_and_rejected.prothermdb: 32,000 thermodynamic measurements, free, no login, but downloads go through a web form rather than an API, and the content is mutant stability for well-studied model proteins. Same organism mismatch as Meltome. The temperature gap this project has is activity at 37 C on a solid polymer, which is not what either database measures
